label: MORNING BRIEF

stories.title: MPs float State ownership of all land
stories.story: Some MPs want the Constitution amended so government can take back land. They say the State spends too much compensating owners before roads are built.
stories.you: It is only an idea for now. Calm worried buyers: titles still stand.

stories.title: Minister: cut 18% loan rates
stories.story: Finance Minister Henry Musasizi said lending rates hover around 18% and told banks to cut them. Bank profits reached Shs2.17 trillion.
stories.you: Rates have not fallen yet. Help buyers compare banks before they borrow.

stories.title: SGR building has not started
stories.story: Works Minister Fred Byamukama told Parliament work on the Shs12.31 trillion railway has not begun. Government aims to have all the money by January 2027.
stories.you: Selling near the line? Price on today’s value, not on a train date.

stories.title: Shs530bn loan for Kanungu roads
stories.story: Government wants to borrow Shs530bn to tarmac 78.4km of roads in Kanungu and Rubanda. Compensation rose from Shs35bn to Shs70bn.
stories.you: Roadside plots there may rise. Check the road reserve before you sell.

stories.title: Bunyonyi road: contractor to go
stories.story: Government is moving to drop Samcrete, which failed to start the 15.8km Kabale–Lake Bunyonyi road. It is part of a Shs112bn roads project.
stories.you: Selling lakeside land? Don’t sell the new road — work has not started.
